newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close up for 4th straight day.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close up for 4th straight day.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed up in shallow trade for the fourth straight day as share prices continued a late January bounce, traders said.
But some analysts fear the rises may be artificial.
With Venezuelan commercial banks offering negative real deposit rates, small domestic investors have poured their savings into local mutual funds.
"It is this money that's keeping the market from a steep correction," said InvestAnalysis consultant Alex Dalmady in a recent research note.

The market's 19-share index gained 0.8 percent to close at 6,417.01 points as a low 14 million shares traded, worth two billion bolivars ($4.2 million), according to preliminary figures from the exchange.

"Hopefully, more positive expectations on the country and the economy can generate some enthusiasm ... and get the market out of its current rut. If not, it's going to be a long year," he added. Last year, the Caracas bolsa was the highest riser in the world, yielding over 100 percent in dollar terms.
Among trade issues, 22 rose, 13 fell and 10 closed flat.
"Although there have been some good company results recently, the bolsa has not responded. It's all down to lack of foreign interest," said one broker.

Among leading stocks, telephone company CANTV edged ahead one bolivar to close at 1901.00, utility Electricidad de Caracas gained 4.00 bolivars to end at 486.00, steel company Sivensa moved ahead 3.00 bolivars to finish at 328.00, and foods producer Mavesa closed up 3.00 bolivars at 160.00
